newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Front-month Brent crude hits record SIMEX high.
newsitem.headline: Front-month Brent crude hits record SIMEX high.

text.p: Front-month Brent crude futures hit a record Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) high in response to the latest clash between the United States and Iraq.
October Brent, the front month, traded at $23.80 per barrel -- its highest level since the market started trading Brent in June last year and one of the highest levels for Brent since the Gulf War.
Front month Brent rose as high as $40.95 in London in 1990 when Iraq invaded Kuwait.
The SIMEX peak was not as high as the London peak overnight Wednesday of $23.82, which was the highest London level since the Gulf War.
Front-month Brent on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) in London hit $23.82 immediately after the news of Iraq's attack.
U.S. military officials said on Wednesday that Iraq fired a surface-to-air missile at two U.S. jet patrolling the northern no-fly zone.
